lead: A hillside neighbourhood with a Romanesque church, a strong community and a park in a former quarry.
text: Its origin is the church of Nostra Senyora del Coll, from the 11th century, with written references from 1099, and until the early 20th century it remained a rural place. The Vallcarca bridge, built in 1923, improved its connections, and in the 1960s it grew at great speed and filled the remaining open spaces.

Today it is a small neighbourhood (0.35 km²) with a strong sense of community, and its best-known corner is the Parc de la Creueta del Coll, created in a former quarry and home to sculptures by Ellsworth Kelly and Eduardo Chillida. At 3,558 €/m² and 906 €/month, it is the most affordable neighbourhood in Gràcia.
housing: Houses and blocks of flats on hillside streets, with areas of low-rise houses.
